name: The Tautira river entrance
place: Tautira, Tahiti, as shown in the painting
evidence: A small fishing figure sits between the broad water and mountain silhouettes in La Farge’s Tautira view.
limit: The painted banks can orient a viewer. The work leaves the point from which the painter judged its distance unspecified.
altText: Pale water lies below green hills. A small figure stands near the middle.
job: the two banks of the trial inlet
stake: A quiet reader needs to recognise the bank mark before the next lantern is lit.
change: The practice river mist takes the east wing out of view.
waitResult: The two river-bank sights ride together on the next-bell clip.
sideResult: The side rail holds its own view of the near bank for the reader who arrives first.
originalTitle: The Entrance to the Tautira River, Tahiti. Fisherman Spearing a Fish
dateKind: The gallery dates the making of this work. It gives no observation time for the game’s practice sights.

name: Meryon’s Collier’s Point etching
place: Te Pātaka o Rākaihautū / Banks Peninsula, Aotearoa New Zealand, as depicted
evidence: Meryon’s etching has a narrow printed landscape and broad margins. The title identifies Collier’s Point.
limit: The collector can keep the plate edge distinct from the edges of the depicted view. The print does not establish checked bearings.
altText: A slim shore view occupies a rectangle in the middle of the printed sheet.
job: the line from the low field
stake: A porter wants the painted headland edge and measured post on separate strips in their tray.
change: The far stop was replaced on a different square when a loose panel was mended.
waitResult: A new notch keeps the old origin visible beside the replacement post.
sideResult: The side strip remains separate, with its low-field origin on its own hook.
originalTitle: Nouvelle Zélande, Presqu'ile de Banks (View of Collier's Point, New Zealand)
dateKind: The gallery dates the making of this work. It gives no observation time for the game’s practice sights.

name: Watkins’s Seal Point photograph
place: Farallon Islands, Pacific Ocean, in the collection title
evidence: Watkins photographed Seal Point with a light sky and many dark marks across the shores of the Farallon Islands.
limit: An image from one position cannot give independent observations behind the points where the shore crosses the view.
altText: Dark forms cluster near both ends of a broad, pale coastal photograph.
stake: The guide wants the first landing strip to show whether the reader can see past the edge of the practice ledge.
change: A low screen covers part of the outer model shore during the morning drill.
waitResult: Both rails carry the new same-bell sight on one reset hook.
sideResult: The side-post fitting lets a waiting visitor use the lower view now.
originalTitle: Seal Point, Farallon Islands, Pacific Ocean
dateKind: The gallery dates Watkins’s photograph to 1879–1880. It is a date range for this particular image.

name: Chien de Garvel, Martinique
place: Martinique, in the collection title
evidence: Paul Emile Miot’s photograph holds a porch edge and seated people in the same frame. The porch rails give a clear near reference.
limit: The camera records one visit. The porch edge cannot identify everyone in the picture or show the area behind the camera.
altText: A photograph with a bright porch railing above foreground figures.
stake: The Harbour has somebody waiting close to its rail. They need a low aim that still leaves the line to the plate open.
change: A replaced foot under the east frame moves its eye to a new ring.
waitResult: The reset pair sits with the replacement frame and its changed start.
sideResult: The side-post guide leaves the narrow porch clip at its old reading height.
dateKind: The gallery dates the making of this work. It gives no observation time for the game’s practice sights.

name: Lear’s Avisavella view
place: Avisavella, Sri Lanka, called Ceylon in the historical title
evidence: Lear’s drawing shows palms and a mid-distance river bank. The collection preserves the spelling Avisavella in the title.
limit: The river bank is visible from one artistic position. This sheet has no measured coordinate for any of the trees.
altText: Clusters of palms frame the water in a pale drawing.
job: the palm silhouettes on the reach
stake: A reader arriving from below the banks can see one of the two practice edges and asks how to find the other.
change: Mist hides the far palms at the time of this trial.
waitResult: The next-bell supports stay paired, with space to keep both banks visible when the screen clears.
sideResult: The new side hook sets the palm strip where the low-rail reader can stand.
medium: gray wash on wove paper, laid down on card
dateKind: The gallery dates the making of this work. It gives no observation time for the game’s practice sights.

name: Rio de Janeiro Bay
place: Rio de Janeiro, Brazil, as depicted
evidence: Heade’s broad bay painting places the horizon behind hills and nearer waves, with a boat in the distance.
limit: The scene gives relative positions in one composition. It gives no harbour depths or an arrival instruction.
altText: A golden bay horizon lies above dark rocks, pale waves and a distant mast.
job: the near wave and far line
stake: At the west dock, a signal held against the near waves should have an origin tied to the far mark.
change: The dock rail moves out one square when a loose clasp is replaced.
waitResult: The pair includes the new rail position and still leaves room for the old sight strip.
sideResult: A side-view guide relieves the wait at the main rail before the next carrier arrives.
dateKind: The gallery dates the making of this work. It gives no observation time for the game’s practice sights.

name: Hut in Trinidad
place: Trinidad, in the collection title
evidence: Hart framed the low roof and shade of this Trinidad scene close to the path in front.
limit: The image gives one visible facing. The roof line cannot show how people used all the space behind it.
altText: A short roof with eaves shades two vertical figures and a path in coloured washes.
stake: The next runner wants to tell where the model path passes out of sight without hiding the roof marks.
change: The far strip arrived with the previous bell marked underneath.
waitResult: A dated pair hangs with the two eaves on a single next-bell clip.
sideResult: The side strip fits at the low courtyard rail with a window still open for the next pair.
dateKind: The gallery dates the making of this work. It gives no observation time for the game’s practice sights.

name: Salt Kettle, Bermuda
place: Salt Kettle, Bermuda, as depicted
evidence: Homer’s painted waterfront puts bright buildings above their pale water reflections, with an open bank at the side.
limit: The reflection shows how the scene looked in this work. It cannot serve as a second independent observer of the bank.
altText: White buildings and trees reflect across turquoise water.
stake: A reader at the Fold thinks the reflection is another observed route mark. The guide can keep the origin of each true sight visible.
change: Haze washes out the far practice building behind the reflector.
waitResult: Both independent sights get their own later marks. The reflected strip stays in a lost-view slot.
sideResult: The side rack gives a clear low angle without using the reflected strip as a second sight.
medium: watercolor over graphite on wove paper
dateKind: The gallery dates the making of this work. It gives no observation time for the game’s practice sights.

name: View of Santiago de Cuba
place: Santiago de Cuba, as depicted
evidence: Homer’s landscape shows roofs above a pale lower slope. Buildings and a farther light ridge overlap in the view.
limit: Roof overlap in this view cannot fix the intervening distance or establish what another observer could see.
altText: A loose sketch of red roofs against a pale backing and farther hills.
job: the overlap of ridge and roofs
stake: A reader needs to see which tall outline belongs to the model roof and which belongs beyond it.
change: A second rooftop strip was caught in the repair clip at the preceding bell.
waitResult: Both roof origins go on a dated rack beside the clear rail.
sideResult: The low side frame keeps the two silhouettes from overlapping for this approach.
medium: watercolor and pen and black ink over graphite on wove paper
dateKind: The gallery dates the making of this work. It gives no observation time for the game’s practice sights.

name: Ship Arkansas leaving Havana
place: Havana, Cuba, in the collection title
evidence: Hashagen’s ship painting puts the Arkansas against other rigging and a low harbour on the same painted line.
limit: The picture is a view of a named departure. It supplies no receipt showing that a later observer used the same direction.
altText: A white-sailed ship sits partly in front of other vessels along a vivid green shoreline.
stake: A harbour helper wants the marker to stay separate from several practice masts.
change: The east rig is standing one square up after a replacement rope was fitted.
waitResult: The next pair records the changed mast post with a fresh date.
sideResult: The side rail gives a new angle that separates the held mark from the other masts.
dateKind: The gallery dates the making of this work. It gives no observation time for the game’s practice sights.

name: Moonlight Effect, Bay of Panama
place: Bay of Panama, as named in the photograph title
evidence: Muybridge’s photograph sets a bright upper patch behind silhouetted boats and harbour forms.
limit: The photograph has a recorded image date. A lighting effect alone cannot establish the time of each depicted arrival.
altText: Dark rigging and low vessels stand against pale light and mottled clouds.
stake: Holders of the night report want the physical dock mark kept separate from the brightness of the view.
change: The east light window closes early and stops at a different bell than the west window.
waitResult: A matched late pair shares one date above the west dock rail.
sideResult: The side-frame sight stays usable while the crew waits for both main windows to open on the same bell.
dateKind: The collection dates this print 1877. That date belongs to the photograph record. The hour of the depicted scene is a different question.

name: Lear’s bend near Philae
place: Philae, Egypt, in the collection title
evidence: Lear’s wash drawing shows water narrowing between dark rocky forms that can hide what lies farther on.
limit: The sheet depicts one view of the rocks. It cannot locate an unseen end of the bend.
altText: Vertical rock faces and reflections enclose water in a grey and brown drawing.
stake: A group needs a guide for the unseen stretch beyond the model rocks, with the original opening mark still visible.
change: The far eye is blocked by a practice baffle fitted against a rock support.
waitResult: The dated register shows when both sights were made after the baffle was lifted.
sideResult: The side rail gives a view from the lower bank and keeps the blocked gap marked.
originalTitle: River Winding through a Rock Formation (Philae, Egypt)
dateKind: The gallery dates the making of this work. It gives no observation time for the game’s practice sights.

name: Mount Serbal from the valley
place: Wádee Feyrán, Egypt, in the historical title
evidence: Francis Frith’s photograph shows a rocky foreground valley between steep far slopes.
limit: One valley view can document foreground and outline. It leaves what would be visible from the ridge unmeasured.
altText: A rocky valley is framed by steep grey ridges in an albumen print.
stake: The Fold guide wants to leave one place to compare the low line with a view from a separate support.
change: One strut changed the east post’s origin when the valley backdrop was tightened.
waitResult: Both replacement marks go on one height-adjusted register.
sideResult: The side-post hanger gives the arriving visitor an angle from beyond the cramped support.
originalTitle: Mount Serbal, from the Wádee Feyrán, Egypt
dateKind: The gallery dates the making of this work. It gives no observation time for the game’s practice sights.

name: Gifford’s Siout painting
place: Siout (Asyut), Egypt, as depicted
evidence: Gifford’s painting sets a pale red ridge far beyond fields and a path. The low light reduces distinctions near the horizon.
limit: The held light belongs to the painted view. It does not document the visibility of the far route at a second bell.
altText: A sun and low ridge sit above an ochre landscape and winding light path.
job: the last light of the path
stake: A carrier wants a checked line on the far edge before the practice landscape dims.
change: The far strip arrived from a brighter bell and gives its own earlier time.
waitResult: Both late marks go under the same date and hold the old brighter strip separately.
sideResult: A guide fits the nearer side eye, where late carriers can compare the current edge.
dateKind: The gallery dates the making of this work. It gives no observation time for the game’s practice sights.

name: Nile Journey, Esneh
place: Esneh (Esna), Egypt, as named in the collection title
evidence: Vedder’s drawing has a low level foreground and a row of trees toward one side. The museum titles it a Nile journey.
limit: A journey drawing preserves a particular framing. The quiet foreground does not establish what lay outside it.
altText: A fine grey drawing with palms to the right and pencil handwriting below.
job: the low foreground and far trees
stake: The shore keeper has a long low board and wants its empty stretch kept visible instead of hidden by the mount.
change: The old east strip comes from another pass of the practice scene, before the lamp was moved.
waitResult: The mount keeps the two fresh strips at the same date and preserves the old journey slip apart.
sideResult: The side guide leaves the low empty stretch accessible for the person arriving now.
medium: black chalk on folded blue paper
dateKind: The gallery dates the making of this work. It gives no observation time for the game’s practice sights.

name: Lear’s Mount Kinchinjunga drawing
place: Kinchinjunga in the record’s name for the mountain scene
evidence: Lear’s drawing layers several ridges. The inscriptions and catalogue identify the view as part of a dated object.
limit: The ridge lines document ordering in one picture. They do not establish the height of each summit.
altText: Fine brown lines outline successive mountain ridges and a low foreground.
stake: The Fold receiver wants to shift two strips until the reading stops separating the wrong ridges.
change: The practice fog screen hides the far marker beside the outer ridge.
waitResult: The new same-bell pair stays on the higher rack to leave the pale ridges visible below.
sideResult: The low side strip holds a line which clears the fog screen on this approach.
medium: gray wash and brush on wove paper
dateKind: The gallery dates the making of this work. It gives no observation time for the game’s practice sights.

name: Arctic Regions photograph 92
place: The Arctic location named The Devil’s Thumb in the published caption
evidence: Dunmore and Critcherson photographed a dark profile partly lost in fog. Their published caption describes a lead among drift ice.
limit: The caption gives the photographers’ account of one passage. It cannot replace a current check of an ice route.
altText: Ice and water meet under a dark shore profile partly covered in haze.
stake: Nobody sends the practice runner past the trays until the keeper can name the sight that can still be used.
change: An opaque screen leaves just the west eye visible.
waitResult: A pair at the next bell keeps both checked leads on the same dated strip.
sideResult: The side guide opens a sheltered line around the practice screen.
originalTitle: The Arctic Regions: No. 92.* The Devil's Thumb partially enveloped in a fog, with the first of the drift Ice from the pack, which was being forced towards the land, from which we escaped through a narrow lead; had we been hemmed in, we should have had to winter there
attribution: John L. Dunmore, and George P. Critcherson
dateKind: The gallery dates this photograph 1869. Its caption describes events of the expedition.

name: The Logan Rock photograph
place: South coast of Cornwall, England, in the collection title
evidence: William May photographed the rock mass from below. A darker face hides what might be seen from the other slope.
limit: This angle records an exposed face. It does not give an all-round outline of the site.
altText: A rocky headland looms from below, with a small block visible near its top.
stake: A reader approaching from below wants the first line kept at their own height.
change: A block support was lifted and the far eye came back on a higher row.
waitResult: The new sight pair stays marked with the relocated foot and keeps the low view line.
sideResult: The side-view mount brings the low approach back into reach without moving the rock block.
originalTitle: The Logan Rock, South Coast of Cornwall
dateKind: The gallery dates the making of this work. It gives no observation time for the game’s practice sights.

name: Boats in a Morning Fog
place: Foggy boat scene in Guérard’s print
evidence: Guérard’s print leaves several boats visible as dim silhouettes surrounded by lighter paper.
limit: Some forms remain visible here. A pale area gives no reliable count of what the print cannot show.
altText: A few faint rigged boats emerge from large areas of light paper.
job: the practice boats behind the veil
stake: Two field readers want to leave the unresolved water squares open until they have enough sight lines.
change: The far post loses its viewing gap when the fog screen rolls down.
waitResult: Two matched sightings after the screen lifts clip to the same bell.
sideResult: The side view leaves today’s lost squares marked and a separate way to check from the lower board.
medium: etching, aquatint, and roulette on simili Japan
dateKind: The gallery dates the making of this work. It gives no observation time for the game’s practice sights.

name: Marée Basse (Low Tide)
place: Tidal scene in Isabey’s print
evidence: Isabey’s print shows vessels and large areas of exposed ground under a textured sky.
limit: The work names a state of the tide. It does not give a repeat reading at another time or the depth at the moment shown.
altText: Tall boats sit against low stripes of ground and an unsettled sky.
stake: The harbour reader needs each sight strip tied to its observed bell before placing a mark at the edge.
change: The east slide still bears the first bell although the practice water line has changed.
waitResult: A matched later pair goes above the dry strip with a new bell mark.
sideResult: The side strip gives the observer a route across the current view without reusing the earlier slide.
dateKind: The gallery dates the making of this work. It gives no observation time for the game’s practice sights.

name: A North East Headland
place: Headland scene as titled by the collection
evidence: Childe Hassam painted sunlit outer ledges that break the coast into several apparent edges.
limit: The way the ledges catch light clarifies one view. It offers no measurement of an edge hidden by another ledge.
altText: Pale rock ledges stand in bright blue water.
stake: The low harbour lamp needs a position reachable from the quieter dock without making the lower gap look checked.
change: The far support has a new square to leave the gap between the ledges open.
waitResult: The guide lays both sights with the displaced post on a larger card.
sideResult: The side-view strip lets one reader use the low mount and keeps the gap named.
dateKind: The gallery dates the making of this work. It gives no observation time for the game’s practice sights.

name: Watchtower on a Cliff with a Stream
place: Cliff and stream scene in Scheuren’s drawing
evidence: Scheuren’s drawing puts a watchtower above irregular rock and trees. The stream passes lower and in front.
limit: The drawing gives the tower relative to nearby features. It does not measure what the tower’s own keeper could see.
altText: A stream and large rocks lead upward toward a small watchtower.
stake: An observer below the frame needs to start their aim at the right point before asking about the tower view.
change: The east stand rests lower than before after a platform was replaced.
waitResult: The two repeat strips share a new bracket and retain the original foot mark.
sideResult: A separate low side post gives the observer another clear line across the practice stream.
originalTitle: Watchtower on a Cliff with a Stream
dateKind: The gallery dates the making of this work. It gives no observation time for the game’s practice sights.

name: Gaskell’s Low Tide print
place: Low tide scene as titled in the collection
evidence: Gaskell’s aquatint holds a curving bright channel between a broad flat foreground and clouded sky.
limit: The paper preserves a channel at one observed stage. Its outer edges do not locate a later wet edge.
altText: A bright curving strip sweeps across a broad, dark foreground under grey clouds.
stake: The first visitor wants to see where two bearings meet before either is reused at the next stage of the practice channel.
change: The far slide gives the channel position from one bell earlier.
waitResult: The keeper ties the repeat lines to their later stage and leaves an empty spot for the next one.
sideResult: The side-view rack can be used at this stage, with its angle marked alongside the old strip.
medium: aquatint in black on wove paper
dateKind: The gallery dates the making of this work. It gives no observation time for the game’s practice sights.

name: Hiroshige’s distant view of Mount Akiha
place: Kakegawa, Japan, as depicted
evidence: Hiroshige places the distant shape behind a bridge used by figures, with several near lines through the foreground.
limit: The print ties a scene to its view. The large near lines cannot give the separate observation needed to fix the mountain’s position.
altText: People cross a bridge in the foreground against an open blue landscape.
job: the bridge eye and far ridge
stake: The Fold group is keeping the near rail name attached to a line that seems to pass through the far ridge.
change: The walkway returns its east stand on a higher row after a joiner changes the bridge rail.
waitResult: The new paired slide reads from the repaired bridge rail without losing the first rail note.
sideResult: The low side mount gives people carrying the strip an extra way to read the far point.
originalTitle: Distant View of Mount Akiha, Kakegawa
dimensions: image: 22.54 × 34.93 cm (8 7/8 × 13 3/4 in.) (approximate dimensions; sealed inside mat)
dateKind: The gallery dates the making of this work. It gives no observation time for the game’s practice sights.

name: Eddystone Lighthouse print
place: Eddystone Rocks, off south-west England, in the print subject
evidence: John Clerk, of Eldin, shows a narrow lighthouse standing over broken water. The tower is one visible mark within the print.
limit: A picture shows the tower at one angle. It gives no independent current bearing or report from another site.
altText: A tall tower stands against a dark sky and water breaking at its base.
stake: The harbour keeper has one easy-to-see practice lamp. A second trace must come from a different marked point.
change: A taller shroud covers the far sight as the two practice lights come on.
waitResult: A second matched bell waits until both lamp windows are open together.
sideResult: The new side mounting carries an independent line around the edge of the shroud.
medium: etching and drypoint on laid paper
dateKind: The gallery dates the making of this work. It gives no observation time for the game’s practice sights.

name: The Buoy (La bouée)
place: Harbour scene in Signac’s work
evidence: Signac’s print shows a red buoy with a broken reflection or colour marks in a rippled harbour view.
limit: The distinct marks are the printmaker’s choices. They cannot locate the buoy for a separate observer on a different day.
altText: A red buoy appears near the bottom of a harbour in blue and yellow marks.
stake: A rail visitor is following the brightest mark. The keeper wants the small measured origin to stay visible too.
change: The recorded east view was clipped at an earlier bell, before the buoy slid one part of the grid.
waitResult: The later pair keeps the new buoy position and its own time beside the old slide.
sideResult: The side guide reaches the new position from the same bell without waiting for the far rail.
dimensions: sheet (trimmed to image): 40.1 x 32.4 cm (15 13/16 x 12 3/4 in.)
dateKind: The gallery dates the making of this work. It gives no observation time for the game’s practice sights.

name: Coast of Brittany
place: Brittany, France, as depicted
evidence: Boudin’s coastal painting gives a broad sky and a low shore with a small mast in the middle distance.
limit: The order of shore, mast and sky is visible in this view. It leaves a mast’s distance and the next weather outside the evidence.
altText: Grey clouds fill much of the view above a low shore and tiny vessels.
stake: A helper needs the small checked marker kept apart from the painted weather background.
change: The tall field has clouded across the far viewing gap.
waitResult: The matching next-bell trace is signed at both posts under the same margin.
sideResult: The side view lets a reader keep the mast on its own line while the tall field stays partly hidden.
dimensions: overall: 47.3 x 66 cm (18 5/8 x 26 in.) framed: 65.1 x 83.8 cm (25 5/8 x 33 in.)
dateKind: The gallery dates the making of this work. It gives no observation time for the game’s practice sights.

name: The Lighthouse at Honfleur
place: Honfleur, France, as depicted
evidence: Seurat paints a narrow light tower beside a pale open stretch and buildings farther along the edge.
limit: The tower is a visible reference in the picture. Its apparent distance cannot locate any observer or measured support.
altText: A pale shore and tower sit beside a small zigzag of fencing.
job: the tower and its nearest fence
stake: The west dock keeper needs the fence and tall tower to separate when viewed from the low rail.
change: A fence repair moves the far sight to the next marked row.
waitResult: The two sights from the new alignment keep the old fence on a dated support card.
sideResult: A side guide works from the low dock and leaves the fence corner free for carriers.
dateKind: The gallery dates the making of this work. It gives no observation time for the game’s practice sights.

name: Fog off Mount Desert
place: Mount Desert Island, Maine, in the collection title
evidence: Church depicts rock and rough light water below a broad haze along the horizon.
limit: The haze is part of a record of what can appear indistinct. It does not give a count of objects beyond the visible edge.
altText: Dark coast rocks face foaming water beneath haze.
stake: A carrier wants the approach squares kept open until the keeper has a pair of sight lines.
change: The far rail has lost its horizon mark behind a chalked screen.
waitResult: The dated pair moves to the shared rail once both sightlines are visible again.
sideResult: The sheltered side eye keeps a record of the current route with the lost horizon still marked.
dateKind: The gallery dates the making of this work. It gives no observation time for the game’s practice sights.

name: Cetara on the Gulf of Salerno
place: Cetara, Italy, as depicted
evidence: Cozens layers high slopes around a view of the Gulf of Salerno and a lower group of features.
limit: The apparent layers indicate what overlaps within this view. The picture does not identify a second observer’s bearings.
altText: A bay is framed by large mountain silhouettes in blue and grey.
job: the outer ridge and inner settlement
stake: The Fold can keep a place for two people at the model ridge, each with a name left next to their sight strip.
change: The far rail’s foot moved slightly to let a visitor turn at the end of the stand.
waitResult: The changed rail position and second clock line stay with the fresh pair.
sideResult: A side guide can leave the turning room open for the visitor who needs it.
originalTitle: Cetara on the Gulf of Salerno
medium: watercolor over graphite on wove paper
dimensions: Overall: 36.6 x 52.7 cm (14 7/16 x 20 3/4 in.) overall (mat size): 61 x 76.2 cm (24 x 30 in.)
dateKind: The gallery dates the making of this work. It gives no observation time for the game’s practice sights.

name: Alpine Huts in Fog
place: Mountain huts in Kirchner’s print
evidence: Angular hut roofs overlap with darker farther hills in Kirchner’s Alpine image, with lighter spaces between.
limit: The print can show an ambiguous boundary for a reader. Light paper does not establish a distance between houses.
altText: Sharp pale roofs and dark hills press into each other in a printed landscape.
stake: The next reader needs a bearing to see between two close bright shapes in the model village.
change: The weather screen covers the outer hut but leaves the lower board clear.
waitResult: The later pair returns to the rack with both roofs named.
sideResult: The side view gives a separate line through the low gap without pretending the covered hut was seen.
dateKind: The gallery dates the making of this work. It gives no observation time for the game’s practice sights.

name: The Tide Rising at Briton Ferry
place: Briton Ferry, Wales, in the collection title
evidence: Sandby pictures the tide rising beneath a broad cloud layer while figures stand on a lower bank.
limit: The title says the tide is rising. The view is not an ordered series giving a changing water height.
altText: Water and a low bank lie beneath a broad pale sky with a few people visible at the edge.
job: the tide and pair of post lines
stake: The trial runner needs the time of water’s edge with both strips before putting the copy on the dock.
change: The incoming east card was clipped when the water was lower, at a different bell.
waitResult: Two new cards stay together with the new water edge and a bell on each strip.
sideResult: The side mount allows the crew to observe today’s edge before the waiting line opens.
originalTitle: The Tide Rising at Briton Ferry
dateKind: The gallery dates the making of this work. It gives no observation time for the game’s practice sights.

name: Pines in a Morning Fog
place: Pine study described in the collection title
evidence: Oehme’s drawing keeps nearby trunks visible while the terrain behind them grows faint.
limit: The drawing distinguishes visible tree forms and pale space. That pale background cannot supply a checked position.
altText: Long thin trees emerge in a warm misty scene.
job: the faint ground near the pines
stake: A viewer on the low rail should be able to see the chosen mark without treating a lost area as empty.
change: The far sight lies behind the model mist while the near woods stay visible.
waitResult: Both west and east readings go on the next-bell clip with the screen position.
sideResult: The low guide holds a separate angle and leaves the obscured area unfilled.
medium: watercolor over graphite on wove paper
dateKind: The gallery dates the making of this work. It gives no observation time for the game’s practice sights.

name: Low Tide at Scheveningen
place: Scheveningen, the Netherlands, as depicted
evidence: Boudin places shore activity and several sails across open ground under a large changing sky.
limit: The title states a stage of the tide. It does not fix measured sightlines or the conditions at a later bell.
altText: Vessels with brown sails sit above broad pale coastal flats.
stake: A crew has room for one strip from either side, and wants their water stage to stay with each.
change: The east record comes from earlier in the practice tide cycle.
waitResult: Both later sights hold their own bell marks alongside the earlier strip.
sideResult: A side rail follows the present sail line from the low approach and marks when it saw it.
dateKind: The gallery dates the making of this work. It gives no observation time for the game’s practice sights.

name: Beacon Rock, Newport Harbor
place: Newport Harbour, Rhode Island, as depicted
evidence: Kensett paints a conspicuous rock face rising close to still water. A smaller distant shape remains along the horizon.
limit: The picture gives near and far references. It cannot fix the position of a boat from one apparent alignment.
altText: A sunlit rock face rises at the right over blue still water.
job: the near beacon and far mark
stake: The harbour wishes to keep its closest name separate from the place where the two strips meet.
change: The far post has been fitted in an alternate socket after the first support cracked.
waitResult: The new channel card names both sound supports and preserves the original origin.
sideResult: The low side board keeps the crossing of the lines visible from where a carrier has both hands busy.
dateKind: The gallery dates the making of this work. It gives no observation time for the game’s practice sights.

name: The Bell Buoy
place: Buoy and sea scene as titled in the collection
evidence: William Trost Richards depicts grey water, a broad sky and a modest buoy or vessel form. The title names the bell buoy.
limit: A picture fixes an angle or weather impression in sight. It does not document an audible observation at the instrument.
altText: Grey water stretches into a pale horizon with a small upright shape.
stake: The Fold has a visitor who needs a visible sign without waiting for a sound check.
change: The far sign was taken at another bell and the keeper has a current mark only from the west.
waitResult: The fresh register keeps the two new angles and the exact later time beside the sound catch.
sideResult: The side guide moves the mark to a visible position for the visitor already at the rail.
medium: watercolor with white highlights over graphite on wove paper
dateKind: The gallery dates the making of this work. It gives no observation time for the game’s practice sights.

name: The Coast of Elba
place: Elba, Italy, as depicted
evidence: Signorini’s monochrome landscape shows the coastline turning across the image before the open sea.
limit: The visible edge offers one change of direction. It does not fix the less visible coastline behind the headland.
altText: A dark coastline sweeps across a narrow image with grey open water.
job: the open bend at the edge
stake: The harbour reader needs to see one place where the next sight can start and where the present trace stops.
change: The far practice bend is behind the weather screen when the trial opens.
waitResult: Two visible ends go on a new dated rack without filling the old missing strip.
sideResult: The side guide opens a separate approach to the practice bend and keeps the missing sight visible as missing.
dateKind: The gallery dates the making of this work. It gives no observation time for the game’s practice sights.

name: Walchensee in Fog
place: Walchensee, Germany, in the collection title
evidence: Corinth’s printed landscape gives some dark branches and buildings while farther scenery is difficult to distinguish.
limit: An obscured line still cannot establish the size of the far bank. The print gives the affected look rather than measured fog.
altText: Dark trees and buildings dissolve into pale areas at the far side.
stake: The low rail reader can see one close point and wants to know what else needs a reading.
change: The east slot loses the next line as the steam screen rises across the distance.
waitResult: The keeper waits for a matched pair and leaves the old faint edge on the blank clip.
sideResult: The side view keeps today’s lost bank and its nearer cross line on separate strips.
medium: lithograph in black on laid paper
dateKind: The gallery dates the making of this work. It gives no observation time for the game’s practice sights.

name: The Gulf of Pozzuoli
place: Pozzuoli, Italy, as depicted
evidence: Schilbach sketches small boats beside the open gulf and an elongated headland extending from the right.
limit: The long point in this view cannot determine which current track would pass near it from the other side.
altText: A warm grey drawing shows boats by a long sweeping shore under open sky.
stake: A reader who can only reach the corner of the stand asks for the paired sight at its lower end.
change: The east post has moved to make the corner passable for a cart.
waitResult: A prepared pair goes on the new stand with a raised mark at its moved start.
sideResult: A side-view caption moves the new sight down to the clear low rail.
medium: watercolor over graphite on wove paper
dateKind: The gallery dates the making of this work. It gives no observation time for the game’s practice sights.

name: Mount’s Bay print
place: Mount’s Bay, Cornwall, England, as depicted
evidence: Haden’s print depicts water, curving foreground and a clouded horizon covered in close etched lines.
limit: The etching’s dense marks give texture. They do not establish how many sight markers were visible farther across the bay.
altText: Dark water marks and foreground shapes run toward a clouded sky.
stake: A receiver is holding a darker tracing over the open bay. They need a place for its limit without blocking the practice reading.
change: Low cloud crosses the far view at the practice bell.
waitResult: The paired return keeps its own clear interval beside the darker earlier trace.
sideResult: The side rail gives a current line from the lower reading station.
dateKind: The gallery dates the making of this work. It gives no observation time for the game’s practice sights.

name: Refitting of a Ship at Low Tide
place: The low-tide workshop scene named in the print title
evidence: Isabey shows a vessel with figures and craft equipment along visible foreground supports.
limit: The sheet depicts work under one named tide condition. Equipment marks do not fix where the workers stood a bell later.
altText: Several steep masts and raised working forms stand in a dark print.
job: the repair work and the shore mark
stake: People from the long deck need the working station named before they can carry the two lines to a helper.
change: The far reading remains in the paint-box clip from the previous bell.
waitResult: The repeat-bell support keeps the worker’s dated first line on a different hook.
sideResult: A side guide stays accessible while work still occupies the far eye.
originalTitle: Radoub d'une Barque à la Marée Basse (Refitting of a Ship at Low Tide)
dateKind: The gallery dates the making of this work. It gives no observation time for the game’s practice sights.
